title: Bubble sort · adjacent swaps
explanation:
Sort [5, 1, 4, 2, 8] from smallest to largest. Compare neighbors, swap if the left value is larger, then move one position right. Each pass places the largest remaining value at the end.

Bar height represents the value; left-to-right position represents array order. Click Next to begin.

Blue = unsorted; amber = compare; red = swap needed; green = final position. Use Next / Previous to follow each move, or click a bar to inspect its value.

steps.title: Sorted · stop after a swap-free pass
steps.explanation:
The result is [1, 2, 4, 5, 8]. Pass 1 settled 8; pass 2 settled 5. Pass 3 made no swaps, proving the remaining neighbors are ordered, so we stop early.

This example used 9 comparisons and 4 swaps across 3 passes.

Algorithm:
For end from n−1 down to 1:
  Set swapped = false.
  For i from 0 to end−1:
    If a[i] > a[i+1], swap them and set swapped = true.
  If swapped is false, stop.

Worst and average time: O(n²). Best time with this early-stop check: O(n). Extra algorithm storage: O(1), since swaps happen in the input array. It is stable when equal values are not swapped. Bubble sort is useful for learning; it is inefficient for large arrays.
